source.text: וַיַּ֨עַל מֹשֶׁ֜ה מֵֽעַרְבֹ֤ת מוֹאָב֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר נְב֔וֹ רֹ֚אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֣י יְרֵח֑וֹ וַיַּרְאֵ֨הוּ יְהוָ֧ה אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֶת־הַגִּלְעָ֖ד עַד־דָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Moses from [the] plains of Moab to [the] mountain of Nebo, [the] top of the Pisgah, which [is] on [the] face of Jericho; and showed him Yahweh all the land, the Gilead as far as Dan,

en.L: And Moses went up from [the] plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, [to the] top of Pisgah, which [is] opposite Jericho. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed him all the land, Gilead as far as Dan,
en.B: Moses climbed from the plains of Moab up Mount Nebo, to the summit of Pisgah, across from Jericho. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
en.R: Moses left the plains of Moab and climbed Mount Nebo to the top of Pisgah, across the river from Jericho. There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} showed him the whole land: Gilead as far north as Dan,

es.L: Y subió Moisés de las llanuras de Moab al monte Nebo, a la cumbre del Pisga, que [está] frente a Jericó. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le mostró toda la tierra, Galaad hasta Dan,
es.B: Moisés subió desde las llanuras de Moab al monte Nebo, a la cima del Pisga, frente a Jericó. Allí {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le mostró toda la tierra: Galaad hasta Dan,
es.R: Moisés salió de las llanuras de Moab y subió al monte Nebo, hasta la cumbre del Pisga, al otro lado del río, frente a Jericó. Allí {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le mostró toda la tierra: Galaad y, hacia el norte, hasta Dan,

fr.L: Et Moïse monta des plaines de Moab au mont Nébo, [au] sommet du Pisga, qui [est] en face de Jéricho. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui fit voir tout le pays, Galaad jusqu’à Dan,
fr.B: Depuis les plaines de Moab, Moïse gravit le mont Nébo jusqu’au sommet du Pisga, face à Jéricho. Là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui montra tout le pays : Galaad jusqu’à Dan,
fr.R: Moïse a quitté les plaines de Moab et il est monté sur le mont Nébo, jusqu’au sommet du Pisga, de l’autre côté du fleuve, en face de Jéricho. Là, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a montré tout le pays : Galaad et, plus au nord, jusqu’à Dan,

sw.L: Na Musa akapanda kutoka nchi tambarare za Moabu hadi mlima Nebo, [hadi] kilele cha Pisga, kilicho mkabala na Yeriko. Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwonyesha nchi yote, Gileadi hadi Dani,
sw.B: Musa alipanda kutoka nchi tambarare za Moabu hadi Mlima Nebo, kwenye kilele cha Pisga, kuelekeana na Yeriko. Huko {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwonyesha nchi yote: Gileadi hadi Dani,
sw.R: Musa aliondoka nchi tambarare za Moabu, akapanda Mlima Nebo hadi kilele cha Pisga, ng'ambo ya mto kuelekea Yeriko. Huko {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwonyesha nchi yote: Gileadi hadi Dani upande wa kaskazini,

decisions.choice: Moses goes up the mountain as the LORD had told him to
decisions.reason: In 32:49-50 the LORD told Moses to climb Mount Nebo, look at the land, and die there; in 3:27 he had told him to climb to the top of Pisgah and look in every direction. This verse carries out those words. Chapter 34 is told by a narrator, not by Moses, and it is the last chapter of Deuteronomy and of the five books of the Law.

decisions.choice: Nebo and Pisgah: a mountain and its high point or ridge in the hills east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Nebo is named as a mountain in the Abarim range in the land of Moab (32:49). Pisgah is a height or ridge on that range (3:17, 27; Numbers 21:20). The verse names both: Moses climbs Mount Nebo and stands on the top of Pisgah. The exact relation of the two names is not certain, but they point to the same lookout over the Jordan valley.

decisions.choice: on the face of Jericho: opposite Jericho, facing it across the Jordan
decisions.reason: "On the face of" a place means facing it. Jericho lay west of the Jordan, so the mountain stood across the river from it.

decisions.choice: Gilead as far as Dan: the view begins in the north-east and runs to the far north
decisions.reason: Verses 1-3 trace the land in a circle: Gilead east of the Jordan up to Dan in the far north, then west across the central tribes to the sea, then south to the Negev and back to the Jordan valley near Jericho. Dan is the northernmost town of the later land of Israel (Judges 18:29; 20:1, "from Dan to Beersheba").

decisions.choice: climbed; summit
decisions.reason: "Went up" and "top" at Literal; Balanced says "climbed" for going up a mountain and "summit", the usual word for its top.

decisions.choice: across the river from Jericho; as far north as Dan
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the river" and "north" so a reader without a map can follow where Moses stands and which way he looks.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("monta", "gravit", "montra") and the passé composé at Readable ("est monté", "a montré"); the narrator's closing comment in verses 10-12, which looks back from a later time, in the passé composé at every level ("il ne s'est plus levé")
decisions.reason: French narrative tense follows the style guide by level; a statement about what has or has not happened up to the narrator's own time is a present perfect in French.

source.text: וְאֵת֙ כָּל־נַפְתָּלִ֔י וְאֶת־אֶ֥רֶץ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וְאֵת֙ כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיָּ֥ם הָאַחֲרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: and all Naphtali, and [the] land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all [the] land of Judah as far as the sea the western,

en.L: and all Naphtali, and [the] land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all [the] land of Judah as far as the western sea,
en.B: all Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the territory of Judah as far as the western sea,
en.R: all the land of Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, and all of Judah as far west as the Mediterranean Sea,

es.L: y todo Neftalí, y [la] tierra de Efraín y de Manasés, y toda [la] tierra de Judá hasta el mar occidental,
es.B: todo Neftalí, el territorio de Efraín y de Manasés, y todo el territorio de Judá hasta el mar occidental,
es.R: toda la tierra de Neftalí, Efraín y Manasés, y todo Judá hasta el mar Mediterráneo, al oeste,

fr.L: et tout Nephtali, et [le] pays d’Éphraïm et de Manassé, et tout [le] pays de Juda jusqu’à la mer occidentale,
fr.B: tout Nephtali, le territoire d’Éphraïm et de Manassé, et tout le territoire de Juda jusqu’à la mer occidentale,
fr.R: tout le pays de Nephtali, d’Éphraïm et de Manassé, et tout Juda jusqu’à la mer Méditerranée, à l’ouest,

sw.L: na Naftali yote, na nchi ya Efraimu na Manase, na nchi yote ya Yuda hadi Bahari ya Magharibi,
sw.B: Naftali yote, eneo la Efraimu na Manase, na eneo lote la Yuda hadi Bahari ya Magharibi,
sw.R: nchi yote ya Naftali, Efraimu na Manase, na Yuda yote hadi Bahari ya Mediterania upande wa magharibi,

decisions.choice: the tribe names stand for the regions those tribes would later hold
decisions.reason: When Moses looks out, the tribes have not yet entered the land. The names describe the regions by the tribes that would settle them (Joshua 15-19): Naphtali in the north, Ephraim and Manasseh in the center, Judah in the south.

decisions.choice: the western sea: the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The word for "western" means "behind" or "last". A person facing east, toward the sunrise, has the west behind him, so "the sea behind" is the sea to the west, the Mediterranean (11:24; Joel 2:20).

decisions.choice: as far west as the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sea its familiar name and adds "west" so the direction is plain; it also says "the land of Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh" so the names are read as regions.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַנֶּ֗גֶב וְֽאֶת־הַכִּכָּ֞ר בִּקְעַ֧ת יְרֵח֛וֹ עִ֥יר הַתְּמָרִ֖ים עַד־צֹֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: and the Negev, and the plain, [the] valley of Jericho, [the] city of the palms, as far as Zoar.

en.L: and the Negev, and the plain, [the] valley of Jericho, [the] city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.
en.B: the Negev, and the plain, the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.
en.R: the Negev in the south, and the Jordan Valley around Jericho, the town of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

es.L: y el Néguev, y la llanura, [el] valle de Jericó, [la] ciudad de las palmeras, hasta Zoar.
es.B: el Néguev, la llanura, el valle de Jericó, la ciudad de las palmeras, hasta Zoar.
es.R: el Néguev en el sur, y el valle del Jordán alrededor de Jericó, la ciudad de las palmeras, hasta Zoar.

fr.L: et le Néguev, et la plaine, [la] vallée de Jéricho, [la] ville des palmiers, jusqu’à Tsoar.
fr.B: le Néguev, la plaine, la vallée de Jéricho, la ville des palmiers, jusqu’à Tsoar.
fr.R: le Néguev au sud, et la vallée du Jourdain autour de Jéricho, la ville des palmiers, jusqu’à Tsoar.

sw.L: na Negebu, na uwanda, bonde la Yeriko, mji wa mitende, hadi Soari.
sw.B: Negebu, uwanda, bonde la Yeriko, mji wa mitende, hadi Soari.
sw.R: Negebu upande wa kusini, na bonde la Yordani kuzunguka Yeriko, mji wa mitende, hadi Soari.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry southern region of the land
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry country south of the hills of Judah (1:7; Numbers 13:17). It closes the southern side of the view.

decisions.choice: the plain: the round, flat floor of the lower Jordan valley, here the part around Jericho
decisions.reason: The word for "plain" means a circle or round area. It names the broad floor of the Jordan valley (Genesis 13:10-12). "The valley of Jericho" says which part of it is meant.

decisions.choice: the city of palm trees is Jericho; Zoar lay near the south end of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Jericho is called "the city of palm trees" again in Judges 1:16 and 2 Chronicles 28:15; it stood at a spring in the valley where palms grew. Zoar was the small town Lot fled to (Genesis 19:22), at the southern edge of the plain. Its exact site is not certain.

decisions.choice: in the south; the Jordan Valley around Jericho
decisions.reason: Readable adds where the Negev lies and names the plain as the Jordan Valley, which is what the Hebrew word refers to here.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו זֹ֤את הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֠שְׁבַּעְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֨ם לְיִצְחָ֤ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְזַרְעֲךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה הֶרְאִיתִ֣יךָ בְעֵינֶ֔יךָ וְשָׁ֖מָּה לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to him, this [is] the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, to your offspring I will give it; I have let you see [it] with your eyes, but there you will not cross over.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "This [is] the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'To your offspring I will give it.' I have let you see [it] with your eyes, but you shall not cross over there."
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "This is the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, when I told them, 'To your descendants I will give it.' I have shown it to you with your own eyes, but you will not go over into it."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "This is the land I made a promise about to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I told them, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' I have let you see it, but you will not go across the river into it."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Esta [es] la tierra que juré a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob, diciendo: “A tu descendencia la daré”. Te la he hecho ver con tus ojos, pero allá no pasarás».
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Esta es la tierra que prometí con juramento a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob, cuando les dije: “Se la daré a tu descendencia”. Te la he mostrado con tus propios ojos, pero no cruzarás hasta ella».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Esta es la tierra que les prometí a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob. Les dije: “Daré esta tierra a tus descendientes”. Te la he dejado ver, pero no cruzarás el río para entrar en ella».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « Ceci [est] le pays que j’ai juré à Abraham, à Isaac et à Jacob, en disant : “À ta descendance je le donnerai.” Je te l’ai fait voir de tes yeux, mais là tu ne passeras pas. »
fr.B: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « Voici le pays que j’ai promis par serment à Abraham, à Isaac et à Jacob, quand je leur ai dit : “Je le donnerai à ta descendance.” Je te l’ai fait voir de tes propres yeux, mais tu n’y entreras pas. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : « C’est le pays que j’ai promis à Abraham, à Isaac et à Jacob. Je leur ai dit : “Je donnerai ce pays à tes descendants.” Je te l’ai laissé voir, mais tu ne traverseras pas le fleuve pour y entrer. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Hii [ndiyo] nchi niliyowaapia Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo, nikisema, 'Uzao wako nitaupa [nchi hii].' Nimekuonyesha [kwa] macho yako, lakini hutavuka kwenda huko."
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Hii ndiyo nchi niliyowaahidi kwa kiapo Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo, nilipowaambia, 'Nitawapa wazao wako nchi hii.' Nimekuonyesha kwa macho yako mwenyewe, lakini hutavuka kuingia humo."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia, "Hii ndiyo nchi niliyowaahidi Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo. Niliwaambia, 'Nitawapa wazao wako nchi hii.' Nimekuacha uione, lakini hutavuka mto kuingia ndani yake."

decisions.choice: the oath the LORD swore to the three fathers
decisions.reason: The promise of the land to Abraham's offspring runs through Genesis (12:7; 13:15; 26:3; 28:13), and Joseph's last words recall it as an oath (Genesis 50:24). Deuteronomy often calls it "the land he swore to your fathers" (1:8; 6:10). Here, at the end, the LORD shows Moses that very land.

decisions.choice: offspring: descendants, the whole line that comes after
decisions.reason: The word means "seed". It is singular in form but stands for all the descendants together. "Your" is singular because the promise was spoken to each father in turn.

decisions.choice: Moses will not enter the land, as the LORD had already said
decisions.reason: The LORD had told Moses he would not cross the Jordan (1:37; 3:26-27; 31:2; 32:52) because of what happened at Meribah (Numbers 20:12). He sees the land but does not enter it.

decisions.choice: promised on oath; descendants
decisions.reason: "Swore" is a solemn promise, so Balanced says "promised on oath" and Readable "made a promise". "Descendants" gives the collective sense of "offspring".

decisions.choice: into it / across the river into it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "there you will not cross". Balanced and Readable say what "there" is, the land; Readable adds the river that Moses would have had to cross.

source.text: וַיָּ֨מָת שָׁ֜ם מֹשֶׁ֧ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֛ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מוֹאָ֖ב עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And died there Moses, [the] slave of Yahweh, in [the] land of Moab, on [the] mouth of Yahweh.

en.L: And Moses, [the] slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, died there in [the] land of Moab, according to the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: There, in the land of Moab, Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} died, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.
en.R: Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, died there in Moab, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said he would.

es.L: Y murió allí Moisés, el esclavo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, en [la] tierra de Moab, conforme a la boca {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Allí, en la tierra de Moab, murió Moisés, el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho.
es.R: Moisés, el siervo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, murió allí en Moab, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho que sucedería.

fr.L: Et Moïse, l’esclave {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, mourut là, dans [le] pays de Moab, selon la bouche {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Là, dans le pays de Moab, mourut Moïse, le serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit.
fr.R: Moïse, le serviteur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, est mort là, dans le pays de Moab, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait annoncé.

sw.L: Na Musa, mtumwa wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akafa huko katika nchi ya Moabu, sawasawa na kinywa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Huko katika nchi ya Moabu, Musa mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikufa, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema.
sw.R: Musa, mtumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, alikufa huko Moabu, kama vile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema angekufa.

decisions.choice: slave of the LORD: one who belongs wholly to the LORD and serves him; here a title of honor
decisions.reason: The word names a person who belongs to a master and works for him, not a hired worker. Said of Moses it is a title of honor: the LORD himself calls him "my servant Moses" (Numbers 12:7-8), and Joshua 1:1-2 begins with the same title. It marks Moses as the one the LORD trusted with his whole house.

decisions.choice: on the mouth of the LORD: at the LORD's word, as he had said
alternatives: by the mouth of the LORD (as if by a kiss), a later Jewish reading
decisions.reason: "On the mouth of" someone means by his word or command (Numbers 3:16; 4:37). Moses dies when and where the LORD had told him he would (32:50). A later Jewish tradition read the phrase as "by the mouth of the LORD", picturing a gentle death "by a kiss"; the ordinary sense of the idiom is "at his word".

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere for Moses (Numbers 12:7), Literal keeps "slave" to show the word's hard edge, and Balanced and Readable say "servant", the fitting word for a trusted man in his master's service.

decisions.choice: as the LORD had said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the idiom by its sense. Readable adds "he would" to show that the LORD had said this beforehand.

source.text: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ר אֹת֤וֹ בַגַּיְ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב מ֖וּל בֵּ֣ית פְּע֑וֹר וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע אִישׁ֙ אֶת־קְבֻ֣רָת֔וֹ עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he buried him in the valley in [the] land of Moab opposite Beth-peor; and not knows anyone his burial place until the day the this.

en.L: And he buried him in the valley in [the] land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor; and no one knows his grave until this day.
en.B: He buried him in the land of Moab, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, and to this day no one knows where his grave is.
en.R: He buried Moses in a valley in the land of Moab, across from Beth-peor. But to this day no one knows where his grave is.

es.L: Y lo enterró en el valle, en [la] tierra de Moab, frente a Bet-peor; y nadie conoce su sepultura hasta este día.
es.B: Lo enterró en la tierra de Moab, en el valle que está frente a Bet-peor, y hasta el día de hoy nadie sabe dónde está su sepultura.
es.R: Enterró a Moisés en un valle de la tierra de Moab, frente a Bet-peor. Pero hasta el día de hoy nadie sabe dónde está su tumba.

fr.L: Et il l’enterra dans la vallée, dans [le] pays de Moab, en face de Beth-Péor ; et personne ne connaît son tombeau jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Il l’enterra dans le pays de Moab, dans la vallée qui fait face à Beth-Péor, et jusqu’à ce jour personne ne sait où se trouve son tombeau.
fr.R: Il a enterré Moïse dans une vallée du pays de Moab, en face de Beth-Péor. Mais aujourd’hui encore, personne ne sait où se trouve sa tombe.

sw.L: Naye akamzika katika bonde katika nchi ya Moabu, mkabala na Beth-peori; wala hakuna mtu ajuaye kaburi lake hadi siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Alimzika katika nchi ya Moabu, katika bonde lililo mkabala na Beth-peori, na hadi leo hakuna mtu ajuaye kaburi lake liko wapi.
sw.R: Alimzika Musa katika bonde moja la nchi ya Moabu, mkabala na Beth-peori. Lakini hadi leo hakuna mtu anayejua kaburi lake liko wapi.

decisions.choice: he buried him: the subject is not named; most likely the LORD, but it may be left unstated
alternatives: he was buried (an unnamed someone buried him)
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and has no named subject. The last one named as acting is the LORD (verse 5, "at the LORD's word"), and it would explain why no one knows the grave: no person buried Moses or saw the place. But Hebrew can also use "he" for an unnamed someone, so the clause may only mean "he was buried". The translation keeps the Hebrew "he" and does not decide.

decisions.choice: singular "he buried" (Hebrew text) against plural "they buried" in some ancient witnesses
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has the singular. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the old Greek translation are generally reported to read "they buried him", making the Israelites the subject. That looks like an attempt to ease the unnamed "he". The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check this against the textual apparatus.

decisions.choice: the valley opposite Beth-peor, where Israel had camped
decisions.reason: Israel camped "in the valley opposite Beth-peor" (3:29; 4:46), and Moses gave his teaching there. The town was linked with the Baal of Peor, the god Israel turned to in Numbers 25:3. Moses is buried near the place where he taught.

decisions.choice: to this day: up to the time the account was written
decisions.reason: The phrase looks back from a later time and says that the grave was still unknown then, so no shrine could be built there.

decisions.choice: he (no deity pronoun marking)
decisions.reason: Because it is not certain that "he" is the LORD, the pronoun is not marked as a pronoun for God, so it does not change with the capitalisation setting. Balanced and Readable begin the sentence with "He", which keeps the Hebrew open. Readable names Moses as the one buried so the two pronouns are not confused.

source.text: וּמֹשֶׁ֗ה בֶּן־מֵאָ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּמֹת֑וֹ לֹֽא־כָהֲתָ֥ה עֵינ֖וֹ וְלֹא־נָ֥ס לֵחֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Moses [was] a son of one hundred and twenty year[s] in his dying; not had grown dim his eye, and not had fled his vigor.

en.L: And Moses [was] a son of 120 years when he died; his eye had not grown dim, and his vigor had not fled.
en.B: Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eyesight had not dimmed, and his strength had not left him.
en.R: Moses was 120 years old when he died. Even then he could still see well, and he was still strong.

es.L: Y Moisés [era] hijo de 120 años cuando murió; no se había oscurecido su ojo, ni había huido su vigor.
es.B: Moisés tenía 120 años cuando murió. Su vista no se había debilitado, ni su vigor lo había abandonado.
es.R: Moisés tenía 120 años cuando murió. Aun así, todavía veía bien y seguía siendo fuerte.

fr.L: Et Moïse [était] fils de 120 ans quand il mourut ; son œil ne s’était pas affaibli, et sa vigueur ne s’était pas enfuie.
fr.B: Moïse avait 120 ans quand il mourut. Sa vue n’avait pas baissé, et sa vigueur ne l’avait pas quitté.
fr.R: Moïse avait 120 ans quand il est mort. Même à cet âge, il voyait encore bien et il était encore fort.

sw.L: Na Musa [alikuwa] mwana wa miaka 120 alipokufa; jicho lake lilikuwa halijafifia, wala uchangamfu wake ulikuwa haujatoweka.
sw.B: Musa alikuwa na umri wa miaka 120 alipokufa. Macho yake yalikuwa hayajafifia, wala nguvu zake hazikuwa zimemwishia.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa na miaka 120 alipokufa. Hata wakati huo bado aliona vizuri, na bado alikuwa na nguvu.

decisions.choice: a son of 120 years: 120 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years. Moses gave his own age as 120 in 31:2.

decisions.choice: vigor: the freshness and strength of life
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root for what is fresh or moist, like green wood (Genesis 30:37). It means the vitality of a living body. Together with his eyesight it says Moses was not worn out by age.

decisions.choice: Moses did not die of weakness or old age
decisions.reason: In 31:2 Moses says he can no longer go out and come in, and gives the LORD's word as the reason he will not cross the Jordan. This verse shows that his death came at the LORD's word (verse 5), not because his body had failed.

decisions.choice: eyesight; strength / could still see well, was still strong
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "eyesight" for "his eye" and "strength" for "his vigor"; Readable turns both into plain statements and adds "even then" to show the contrast with his great age.

source.text: וַיִּבְכּוּ֩ בְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּעַֽרְבֹ֥ת מוֹאָ֖ב שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים י֑וֹם וַֽיִּתְּמ֔וּ יְמֵ֥י בְכִ֖י אֵ֥בֶל מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And wept [the] sons of Israel Moses in [the] plains of Moab thirty days; and were completed [the] days of weeping of [the] mourning of Moses.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel wept [for] Moses in [the] plains of Moab thirty days; and the days of weeping [in the] mourning for Moses were completed.
en.B: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} wept for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, until the days of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cried over Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days. Then their time of mourning for him was over.

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel lloraron a Moisés en [las] llanuras de Moab treinta días; y se cumplieron los días del llanto [del] duelo por Moisés.
es.B: Los israelitas lloraron a Moisés en las llanuras de Moab durante treinta días, hasta que se cumplieron los días de llanto y de duelo por Moisés.
es.R: Los israelitas lloraron por Moisés en las llanuras de Moab durante treinta días. Después terminó su tiempo de duelo por él.

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël pleurèrent Moïse dans [les] plaines de Moab trente jours ; et les jours des pleurs [du] deuil de Moïse s’achevèrent.
fr.B: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} pleurèrent Moïse dans les plaines de Moab pendant trente jours, jusqu’à ce que s’achèvent les jours de pleurs et de deuil pour Moïse.
fr.R: Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont pleuré Moïse dans les plaines de Moab pendant trente jours. Puis le temps du deuil pour lui s’est terminé.

sw.L: Na wana wa Israeli wakamlilia Musa katika nchi tambarare za Moabu siku thelathini; na siku za kulia [katika] maombolezo ya Musa zikatimia.
sw.B: Waisraeli walimlilia Musa katika nchi tambarare za Moabu kwa siku thelathini, hadi siku za kulia na kumwombolezea Musa zilipokwisha.
sw.R: Waisraeli walimlilia Musa katika nchi tambarare za Moabu kwa siku thelathini. Kisha muda wao wa kumwombolezea ukaisha.

decisions.choice: thirty days: a full period of mourning, as for Aaron
decisions.reason: Israel mourned Aaron for thirty days too (Numbers 20:29). It is a full, public mourning for a leader of the whole people.

decisions.choice: the days of weeping of the mourning of Moses: the time of weeping that mourning for Moses called for
decisions.reason: The three nouns are linked in a chain. The weeping belongs to the mourning, and the mourning is for Moses. When those days ended, the people could move on under Joshua (verse 9; Joshua 1:1-2).

decisions.choice: until ... came to an end / Then ... was over
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two clauses with "until" to show that the weeping lasted for the whole period; Readable makes two sentences. Readable says "cried", the everyday word for weeping.

source.text: וִֽיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֗וּן מָלֵא֙ ר֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֔ה כִּֽי־סָמַ֥ךְ מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־יָדָ֖יו עָלָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁמְע֨וּ אֵלָ֤יו בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joshua son of Nun [was] full [of the] spirit of wisdom, for had laid Moses his hands on him; and listened to him [the] sons of Israel and did just as commanded Yahweh Moses.

en.L: And Joshua son of Nun [was] full of [the] spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him; and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel listened to him and did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.B: Joshua son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, since Moses had laid his hands on him. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} obeyed him, doing what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.
en.R: Moses had placed his hands on Joshua son of Nun, and so Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} listened to Joshua and obeyed him. They did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses.

es.L: Y Josué hijo de Nun [estaba] lleno del espíritu de sabiduría, porque Moisés había puesto sus manos sobre él; y los hijos de Israel lo escucharon e hicieron tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Moisés.
es.B: Josué hijo de Nun estaba lleno del espíritu de sabiduría, pues Moisés le había impuesto las manos. Los israelitas le obedecieron e hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había mandado a Moisés.
es.R: Moisés había puesto sus manos sobre Josué hijo de Nun, y por eso Josué quedó lleno del espíritu de sabiduría. Los israelitas escucharon a Josué y le obedecieron. Hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había dicho a Moisés.

fr.L: Et Josué, fils de Nun, [était] rempli de l’esprit de sagesse, car Moïse avait posé ses mains sur lui ; et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël l’écoutèrent et firent comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait commandé à Moïse.
fr.B: Josué, fils de Nun, était rempli de l’esprit de sagesse, car Moïse lui avait imposé les mains. Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} lui obéirent et firent ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait ordonné à Moïse.
fr.R: Moïse avait posé ses mains sur Josué, fils de Nun, et c’est pourquoi Josué a été rempli de l’esprit de sagesse. Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont écouté Josué et lui ont obéi. Ils ont fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait dit à Moïse.

sw.L: Na Yoshua mwana wa Nuni [alikuwa] amejaa roho ya hekima, kwa maana Musa alikuwa ameweka mikono yake juu yake; na wana wa Israeli wakamsikiliza, wakafanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru Musa.
sw.B: Yoshua mwana wa Nuni alikuwa amejaa roho ya hekima, kwa kuwa Musa alikuwa ameweka mikono yake juu yake. Waisraeli walimtii, wakafanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru Musa.
sw.R: Musa alikuwa ameweka mikono yake juu ya Yoshua mwana wa Nuni, na kwa sababu hiyo Yoshua alijazwa roho ya hekima. Waisraeli walimsikiliza Yoshua na kumtii. Walifanya yale ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwambia Musa.

decisions.choice: the spirit of wisdom: wisdom given by God for the task of leading
alternatives: the Spirit of wisdom (God's own Spirit)
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the craftsmen God filled for making the priests' clothes (Exodus 28:3) and of the coming king (Isaiah 11:2). Whether "spirit" here means God's own Spirit or a gift of wisdom he gives is not certain; either way the wisdom comes from God. Numbers 27:18 calls Joshua "a man in whom is spirit".

decisions.choice: laying hands on Joshua: the act that passed Moses' authority to him
decisions.reason: In Numbers 27:18-23 the LORD told Moses to lay his hand on Joshua before the priest and the whole congregation and to give him some of his authority. The verse links Joshua's wisdom with that commissioning.

decisions.choice: listened to him: obeyed him
decisions.reason: To "listen to" a leader means to do what he says. The people obey Joshua, and in doing so they keep the commands the LORD gave through Moses.

decisions.choice: obeyed him / listened to Joshua and obeyed him
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense, "obeyed". Readable keeps "listened" and adds "obeyed", and names Joshua so the reader does not take "him" to mean Moses.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־קָ֨ם נָבִ֥יא ע֛וֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כְּמֹשֶׁ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יְדָע֣וֹ יְהוָ֔ה פָּנִ֖ים אֶל־פָּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And not has arisen a prophet again in Israel like Moses, whom knew him Yahweh face to face,

en.L: And there has not risen again in Israel a prophet like Moses, one whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} knew face to face,
en.B: Never again has Israel had a prophet like Moses, one {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} knew face to face,
en.R: Israel has never had another prophet like Moses. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} knew him face to face.

es.L: Y no se ha levantado más en Israel un profeta como Moisés, a quien {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} conoció cara a cara,
es.B: Nunca más ha tenido Israel un profeta como Moisés, a quien {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} conocía cara a cara,
es.R: Israel nunca ha tenido otro profeta como Moisés. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo conocía cara a cara.

fr.L: Et il ne s’est plus levé en Israël de prophète comme Moïse, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} connaissait face à face,
fr.B: Israël n’a plus jamais eu de prophète comme Moïse, lui que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} connaissait face à face,
fr.R: Israël n’a jamais eu d’autre prophète comme Moïse. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le connaissait face à face.

sw.L: Wala hajainuka tena katika Israeli nabii kama Musa, ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjua uso kwa uso,
sw.B: Tangu hapo Israeli hawajapata tena nabii kama Musa, ambaye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjua uso kwa uso,
sw.R: Israeli hawajawahi kuwa na nabii mwingine kama Musa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjua uso kwa uso.

decisions.choice: no later prophet has equaled Moses, though one like him had been promised
decisions.reason: In 18:15-18 Moses said the LORD would raise up a prophet like him from among the people. The narrator looks back from a later time and says no prophet since has been his equal. So the closing words of the Law both honor Moses and leave that promise still waiting.

decisions.choice: knew face to face: knew him directly and closely, without a go-between
decisions.reason: The LORD spoke with Moses "face to face, as a man speaks with his friend" (Exodus 33:11), "mouth to mouth" and not in riddles (Numbers 12:6-8). To "know" here is personal knowledge: the LORD chose Moses and dealt with him closely (Exodus 33:12, 17).

decisions.choice: verses 10-12 close the five books of the Law
decisions.reason: These are the last words of Deuteronomy and of the whole Torah. They sum up Moses' life by his unique nearness to the LORD (verse 10) and by the deeds the LORD did through him (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: ends with a comma
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on through verses 11 and 12, which say in what ways Moses was unequaled, so Literal and Balanced end this verse with a comma. Readable makes shorter sentences in each verse.

source.text: לְכָל־הָ֨אֹת֜וֹת וְהַמּוֹפְתִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר שְׁלָחוֹ֙ יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לְפַרְעֹ֥ה וּלְכָל־עֲבָדָ֖יו וּלְכָל־אַרְצֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: for all the signs and the wonders which sent him Yahweh to do in [the] land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,

en.L: for all the signs and the wonders which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent him to do in [the] land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,
en.B: none like him in all the signs and wonders {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent him to do in the land of Egypt, against Pharaoh, all his officials and his whole land,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent Moses to Egypt to do all those signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his officials and his whole country. No other prophet has done anything like them.

es.L: por todas las señales y los prodigios que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo envió a hacer en [la] tierra de Egipto, al faraón y a todos sus siervos y a toda su tierra,
es.B: ninguno como él en todas las señales y prodigios que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo envió a hacer en la tierra de Egipto, contra el faraón, todos sus funcionarios y toda su tierra,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} envió a Moisés a Egipto para hacer todas aquellas señales y prodigios contra el faraón, todos sus funcionarios y todo su país. Ningún otro profeta ha hecho nada parecido.

fr.L: pour tous les signes et les prodiges que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’envoya faire dans [le] pays d’Égypte, à Pharaon et à tous ses serviteurs et à tout son pays,
fr.B: nul comme lui pour tous les signes et les prodiges que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’envoya accomplir dans le pays d’Égypte, contre Pharaon, tous ses hauts fonctionnaires et tout son pays,
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait envoyé Moïse en Égypte pour faire tous ces signes et ces prodiges contre Pharaon, tous ses ministres et tout son pays. Aucun autre prophète n’a jamais rien fait de semblable.

sw.L: kwa ishara zote na maajabu ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtuma kuyafanya katika nchi ya Misri, kwa Farao na kwa watumishi wake wote na kwa nchi yake yote,
sw.B: hakuna kama yeye katika ishara zote na maajabu ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtuma kuyafanya katika nchi ya Misri, dhidi ya Farao, maafisa wake wote na nchi yake yote,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtuma Musa Misri kufanya ishara hizo zote na maajabu dhidi ya Farao, maafisa wake wote na nchi yake yote. Hakuna nabii mwingine aliyefanya jambo lolote kama hayo.

decisions.choice: for all the signs: in respect of all the signs; it says how Moses was unequaled
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb of its own. It goes on from verse 10: no prophet has been like Moses with regard to all the signs and wonders. The connecting word here means "with regard to", not "because".

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: acts of power that showed the LORD at work and carried his message
decisions.reason: The pair is Deuteronomy's name for the plagues and the rescue from Egypt (4:34; 6:22; 7:19; 26:8; Exodus 7:3). A sign points to something beyond itself; a wonder is a striking, unusual event.

decisions.choice: the LORD sent Moses to do them
decisions.reason: The deeds are the LORD's; Moses did them because he was sent (Exodus 3:10-12; 4:21). The honor given to Moses in these verses rests on what the LORD did through him.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" here are the men of his court. Literal says "servants"; Balanced and Readable say "officials", which names their position.

decisions.choice: none like him in ... against Pharaoh / No one else did ... Moses did them to
decisions.reason: Balanced repeats "none like him" so the verse reads on from verse 10, and says "against" for the "to" of the deeds done to Pharaoh. Readable makes its own sentences, names Moses, and says "no other prophet has done anything like them" to carry on the comparison from verse 10.

source.text: וּלְכֹל֙ הַיָּ֣ד הַחֲזָקָ֔ה וּלְכֹ֖ל הַמּוֹרָ֣א הַגָּד֑וֹל אֲשֶׁר֙ עָשָׂ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and for all the hand the strong and for all the terror the great which did Moses to [the] eyes of all Israel.

en.L: and for all the strong hand and for all the great terror which Moses did before [the] eyes of all Israel.
en.B: and in all the mighty power and all the great and terrifying deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
en.R: No one else has ever shown such mighty power or done such great and terrifying things as Moses did while all Israel watched.

es.L: y por toda la mano fuerte y por todo el gran terror que hizo Moisés ante [los] ojos de todo Israel.
es.B: y en todo el gran poder y todos los hechos grandes y terribles que Moisés realizó a la vista de todo Israel.
es.R: Nadie más ha mostrado jamás un poder tan grande ni ha hecho cosas tan grandes y terribles como las que hizo Moisés mientras todo Israel miraba.

fr.L: et pour toute la main forte et pour toute la grande terreur que Moïse fit sous [les] yeux de tout Israël.
fr.B: et pour toute la grande puissance et toutes les actions grandes et terrifiantes que Moïse accomplit sous les yeux de tout Israël.
fr.R: Personne d’autre n’a jamais montré une telle puissance, ni fait des choses aussi grandes et terrifiantes que celles que Moïse a faites devant tout Israël.

sw.L: na kwa mkono wote wenye nguvu na kwa utisho wote mkuu ambao Musa aliufanya mbele ya macho ya Israeli wote.
sw.B: na katika uweza wote mkuu na matendo yote makuu ya kutisha ambayo Musa aliyafanya machoni pa Israeli wote.
sw.R: Hakuna mwingine aliyewahi kuonyesha uweza mkubwa kama huo au kufanya mambo makuu ya kutisha kama aliyoyafanya Musa, Israeli wote wakitazama.

decisions.choice: the strong hand: great power at work
decisions.reason: "A strong hand" is Deuteronomy's phrase for the LORD's power in bringing Israel out of Egypt (4:34; 5:15; 26:8). Here it is said of Moses, because the LORD's power worked through him (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the great terror: awe-inspiring deeds that made people afraid
decisions.reason: The word means fear or terror, and here the things that caused it. Deuteronomy 4:34 and 26:8 pair it with "a strong hand" for the events of the exodus.

decisions.choice: before the eyes of all Israel: the Law ends where it began, with all Israel
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy began with the words Moses spoke "to all Israel" (1:1), and the five books of the Law end with what he did "before the eyes of all Israel". The whole people were witnesses.

decisions.choice: mighty power; great and terrifying deeds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "strong hand" and turn "great terror" into the deeds that caused it. Readable repeats "no one else" so the verse stands on its own as a sentence.
